Yes. DrCertificate connects people with migraine to certified MBBS, MD or MS doctors who review a request through a digital chat consultation. The doctor decides whether to issue a medical certificate for migraine, and an approved certificate arrives as a PDF by email. The service is for non emergency cases and is not for India, legal or insurance use.
Before you apply
What is a medical certificate for migraine?
A medical certificate for migraine is a document from a certified doctor confirming that, in the doctor's view, you need rest or adjusted work because of a migraine attack.
Most people with migraine choose a sick leave certificate or a work from home certificate. You usually show it to an employer, a university or a school to explain an absence.

The certificate does not come with a diagnosis or treatment plan from DrCertificate. The platform connects you with independent doctors and does not diagnose, treat or prescribe. Migraine is classed as a neurological condition under ICD-10 code G43 in the International Classification of Diseases, so a doctor can accept it as a genuine reason for time off. The decision to issue still rests with the doctor.
Which kinds of migraine can a doctor consider online?

A doctor on DrCertificate can consider a common migraine attack when the symptoms are familiar to you and no warning signs are present. The doctor decides whether rest is needed and for how long, based on what you share in the consultation.
No fixed number of days is promised.
Migraine attacks usually last between 4 hours and 3 days, according to the NHS. That window helps a doctor judge what rest, if any, fits your attack.

Not every form of migraine suits a chat consultation. A first ever severe headache, a migraine that brings weakness on one side of the body, or any attack with the warning signs listed further down needs a doctor in person.

items: Migraine without aura The most common type, marked by a severe, throbbing headache on one side of the head.
Migraine with aura Visual changes like flashing lights or zigzag lines appear before or during the headache.
Chronic migraine Headaches on 15 or more days a month. A doctor looks at the current attack you describe.
Vestibular migraine Dizziness and balance problems, with or without head pain.

blocks.text: What should you tell the doctor about your migraine?
Tell the doctor what your migraine feels like, when it started and how it affects your day. Clear, honest details help the doctor decide whether a certificate fits your situation.
Vague answers slow things down.

items: Symptoms Throbbing head pain, which side it is on, nausea and vomiting, sensitivity to light or sound, and any aura.
Onset and duration The date the attack began, how long it has lasted and whether it matches past attacks.
Severity Whether you can look at a screen, travel or work right now.
Earlier records Any past diagnosis, scan result or neurologist's note you already have.
Leave requested The dates you are asking the certificate to cover.

blocks.text: When is migraine not suitable for an online certificate?

Migraine is not suitable for an online certificate when it comes with signs of an emergency. Call your local emergency number or go to a hospital if you notice any of the signs listed here, which the NHS names as reasons to seek emergency care.
DrCertificate is for suitable non emergency situations and does not diagnose, treat or prescribe. A doctor may decline any request that cannot be safely assessed by chat.

items: Sudden, intense headache A headache that came on suddenly and is severely painful.
Speech or memory problems Trouble speaking or remembering things.
Loss of vision Partial or total loss of sight.
Seizure Any fit or seizure during the attack.
One sided weakness Weakness in the arm or leg on one side of the body.

What happens if the doctor does not issue a certificate for migraine?

The doctor alone decides whether to issue a certificate, and that decision is independent of DrCertificate. A request may not suit chat when the name and ID do not match, when the symptoms and details shared are inconsistent, or when warning signs point to in person care.
If the doctor declines, the payment is not refunded.

blocks.text: Questions about medical certificates for migraine
Can I share test results or a neurologist's report for my migraine?

Yes, you can mention any earlier diagnosis, scan result or neurologist's note when you describe your migraine in the online form. Those details help the doctor understand your history. Tests are not always needed for migraine, and the doctor decides based on the full picture you share.
How many days off can I get for a migraine?

The doctor decides the leave period, if any, after the chat consultation. In most South East Asian countries, sick leave and work from home notes go up to 7 days for generic symptoms. The NHS says migraine attacks usually last between 4 hours and 3 days, which guides the rest a doctor may suggest.
Will my employer accept an online medical certificate for migraine?

Your employer decides whether to accept an online medical certificate. Every doctor on DrCertificate is registered with a medical council, but workplace policies differ between companies and countries. Check with your HR team or university office that they accept online medical notes before you apply, since payments are non refundable.
Can I have a video call or see a doctor in person?

No. DrCertificate does not offer video or in person consultations. A certified doctor reviews your request through a digital chat consultation only. If your migraine needs a physical examination, or you would prefer to speak with someone face to face, please visit a local clinic or hospital.
What should I do if my migraine gets worse after I apply?

Seek urgent in person care if your headache becomes sudden and intensely painful, or if you develop trouble speaking, vision loss, a seizure or weakness on one side of the body. Do not wait for a certificate. A chat consultation cannot replace emergency treatment, so call your local emergency number.
Is migraine a valid reason for a medical certificate?

Yes, migraine is a recognised neurological condition, listed under ICD-10 code G43 in the International Classification of Diseases. A migraine attack can bring severe head pain, nausea and vomiting that make work or study hard. A certified doctor still decides whether your symptoms justify a certificate after reviewing your request.
How fast will I receive my migraine certificate?

An approved medical certificate for migraine usually arrives by email as a PDF in about 30 minutes. The clock starts once your form and Stripe payment are complete. If the doctor asks for more details in the chat, replying quickly keeps your review moving.
